title: Those Who Retire a Decade Before They Retire
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The article names a familiar workplace phenomenon: tenured employees who mentally check out years before their actual retirement, showing up for attendance but not contribution. It traces the behavioral pattern precisely, from withdrawing opinions in meetings to quietly deferring leadership to others, and warns that this disengagement is especially corrosive on small teams where every person's output matters. Rather than treating this as an inevitable late-career phase to be tolerated, the piece frames it as a leadership failure of omission, arguing that leaders who don't actively re-engage a coasting veteran are implicitly signing off on their disengagement. The remedy proposed is direct: assign ownership, accountability, and visible responsibility rather than letting the person drift.
points: Disengaged tenured employees often keep showing up but stop contributing, a pattern the piece calls being retired before you retire.
The damage from one disengaged veteran is proportionally worse on small teams, where every person's output is load-bearing.
Leaders who leave a coasting veteran alone are implicitly granting permission for the disengagement to continue.
The fix is active reassignment of ownership — putting the person back in charge of initiatives and holding them to milestones — rather than quiet tolerance.
quotes: Unfortunately for everyone around them, their engagement primarily consists of attendance, not contribution.
The signs are plain to see for those interested in catching this cancer early before it metastasizes.
They start to refrain from offering opinions or viewpoints, often sitting quietly through meetings as passive observers.
Good leaders don’t accept the early retiree’s new reality. They put them in charge of key initiatives and projects and hold them accountable to critical milestones.
As the popular poster says, “Growing old is mandatory but giving up is optional.
Leaders who leave them alone offer implicit permission to do so. So, who retired early?
